flawed_step: The claim that some single Kempe-chain interchange always frees a color at a degree-5 vertex (Kempe's flawed argument); chains can simultaneously block all single interchanges.
counterexample: G: vertices v,w1..w5; edges v-wi (i=1..5), cycle w1w2,w2w3,w3w4,w4w5,w5w1, plus chords w2w5,w3w5 (planar: v inside pentagon, both chords outside sharing w5). Coloring of G-v: w1=1,w2=2,w3=3,w4=1,w5=4 (proper). Kempe chains: (1,2): {w1,w2},{w4}; (1,3): {w3,w4},{w1}; (1,4): {w1,w4,w5}; (2,3): {w2,w3}; (2,4): {w2,w5}; (3,4): {w3,w5}. Neighbor colors after each swap: 2,1,3,1,4 / 1,2,3,2,4 / 1,2,1,3,4 / 3,2,3,1,4 / 4,2,3,4,1 / 1,3,2,1,4 / 1,4,3,1,2 / 1,2,4,1,3 — all four colors remain in every case.
assessment_summary: Explicit 6-vertex planar graph with a degree-5 vertex and a proper 4-coloring of G-v using all four colors on N(v); exhaustive check of all 8 Kempe chains shows no single interchange reduces the neighbor colors to three. Statement is false.
